issue-session.description: Give `user` a new live session and capture its cookie value (the credential), by whatever means the core's tests use. The credential is made up and never a real one.

expire-session.description: Move the session's expiry into the past, as time passing would.

revoke-session.description: Revoke the session on the core, as signing out elsewhere or an administrator would.

csrf-for.description: Capture the CSRF token the core derives for that session, by the core's own derivation (a test hook, never a production route).

core-degraded.description: Make the core unable to answer lookups until `core-recovered`.

basic.description: One core with a service token, an origin allow-list of one entry, and two users. Every name, origin and id is made up. A session's credential is captured from `issue-session`; no case assumes any credential or id.
basic.service_token: a per-deployment secret the runner holds; `valid` sends it, `wrong` sends a different string
